justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 and the brief via Catalog Management Component for physical and digital items, Digital Content Repository for DRM content, Circulation Engine Component for lending, and Circulation & Self-Service Component for patron interactions.
justifications.performance_efficiency: R-05 is explicitly targeted using a dedicated Search Engine (Elasticsearch) with tuned Query Parser and Lucene storage, client-side debouncing and caching via TanStack Query, and asynchronous event indexing via Search Synchronizer Component and RabbitMQ.
justifications.compatibility: Seamless interoperability is established with external systems, including Digital Content Repository / DRM Provider via LTI/OAuth and REST, Payment Gateway, Notification Service via HTTPS/REST in Integration Worker, and external EU-compliant Identity Providers.
justifications.usability: Library Patron and Librarian personas are explicitly catered to through Routing & Shell Component, Catalog & Search Component, and Circulation & Self-Service Component within the Web Application, providing tailored self-service and administrative portals.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is well-supported through RabbitMQ Quorum Queues, Dead Letter Handler, Retry & Dead-Letter Handler in Integration Worker, and PgBouncer connection pooling, though explicit high-availability clustering and disaster recovery topologies are not fully elaborated.
justifications.security: EU data residency is enforced via Audit & Data Residency Enforcement Module, LUKS disk encryption, and EU-compliant IdP. The API Gateway manages JWT authentication and TLS termination, complemented by TLS 1.3 across internal messaging and database transports.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture displays clear modularity and low coupling. Core Domain, Search Engine, and Integration Worker are decoupled asynchronously via RabbitMQ, with fine-grained component boundaries in Spring Boot and React facilitating independent updates and maintainability.
justifications.portability: Components use standard, portable runtime technologies (Node.js, Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ). While container runtimes or Kubernetes orchestration are not explicitly defined, the technology choices avoid vendor lock-in and readily support EU-restricted infrastructure.

PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch cluster and client-side debouncing support low latency, though proxying search queries through Core Domain rather than directly via API Gateway adds avoidable processing overhead under peak load.
sensitivity_points: Throughput and connection limits in Core Domain proxying searches to Elasticsearch
Elasticsearch index shard allocation and memory sizing
tradeoffs: Routing searches via Core Domain enforces domain policies but increases processing latency

PERF-02.justification: Search reads are decoupled from transactional updates using Elasticsearch and asynchronous messaging, easily meeting the 5-minute index SLA without degrading read performance, though dual indexing paths create architectural ambiguity.
sensitivity_points: Indexing pipeline lag under high concurrent catalog update volumes
tradeoffs: Near real-time eventual consistency reduces database contention at the cost of immediate visibility

AVAIL-01.justification: Circulation transactions are isolated in PostgreSQL and will not be lost. However, clustering, replica sets, and automated failover for the Search Engine are not explicitly specified to guarantee sub-minute search recovery.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch replica count and master node quorum configuration
tradeoffs: High replica counts improve availability and read throughput but increase storage costs

AVAIL-02.justification: Stateless React client delivery backed by API Gateway SSL termination and proxying allows seamless rerouting across front-end instances, while PostgreSQL transactional boundaries safeguard in-flight loan state.
sensitivity_points: Health check interval and failover detection latency in API Gateway
tradeoffs: Stateless front-end simplifies horizontal failover but relies heavily on token-based re-authentication

MOD-01.justification: Although Level 1 links to a Digital Content Repository, the lower-level containers and components lack a dedicated digital provider adapter or connector component, requiring modification to core domain catalog components.
sensitivity_points: Absence of modular plug-in architecture for external catalog ingest adapters
tradeoffs: Hardcoding catalog integration in Core Domain reduces initial complexity but impedes provider extensibility

MOD-02.justification: Circulation rules and invariants are encapsulated directly within the Spring Boot/TX Circulation Engine Component without an externalized business rules engine or dynamic configuration mechanism.
sensitivity_points: Coupling of circulation business logic to compiled Java code
tradeoffs: Embedding rules in application code ensures type safety but mandates redeployment for policy updates

SEC-01.justification: EU data residency is explicitly addressed via dedicated database modules, EU-hosted PostgreSQL, and LUKS-encrypted index nodes, although external notification and payment integrations require operational data-routing governance.
sensitivity_points: Compliance enforcement across external third-party SaaS providers like SendGrid and Twilio
tradeoffs: Restricting data storage to EU regions satisfies regulatory compliance but limits third-party provider options

SEC-02.justification: Authentication & Authorization Filter at API Gateway inspects JWTs and Core Domain validates loan invariants, while the PostgreSQL Audit module records actions, ensuring unauthorized reads are denied and auditable.
sensitivity_points: Granular patron identity validation in domain authorization filters to prevent IDOR attacks
tradeoffs: Deep audit logging across database transactions ensures accountability but adds storage and I/O overhead
